exercises.title: Sing a Song of Sixpence
exercises.instructions:
Sing a song of sixpence.
A pocket full of rye,
Four and twenty blackbirds,
Baked in a pie.
When the pie was opened,
The birds began to sing.
Wasn't that a dainty dish,
To set before the King?
The King was in his counting house,
Counting out his money.
The Queen was in the parlour,
Eating bread and honey.
The maid was in the garden,
Hanging out the clothes,
When down came a blackbird,
And pecked at her nose!
Sing the rhyme together.
Walk around like a King or Queen.
Flap your arms like the wings of a blackbird – fly around the room.
Make a beak with your thumb and first finger. Peck your beaks using both hands.
Reach down for some pegs and pretend to peg the clothes onto the line.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some of the rhyme and attempts a few actions such as walking, flapping arms, pecking with fingers or reaching for pegs. Needs significant support to follow the sequence of movements and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including walking like a King or Queen, flying like a blackbird, making a beak with fingers, and pretending to peg clothes on a line. May need reminders to coordinate movements, follow instructions, or complete the full sequence.

Performs most actions correctly and in sequence. Walks with control, flaps arms to imitate flight, uses fingers effectively to make a beak and peck, reaches and stretches to peg clothes on the line, and lies quietly on their back while counting to 5 with minimal support.

Performs all actions confidently and accurately throughout the rhyme. Walks expressively like a King or Queen, flies smoothly like a blackbird, coordinates finger movements to make and use a beak, reaches and stretches effectively when pegging clothes, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting to 5.

exercises.title: The Hokey-Cokey
exercises.instructions:
You put your left arm in,
Your left arm out.
In, out, in, out,
You shake it all about.
You do the hokey-cokey,
And you turn around.
That's what it's all about.
Oh, the hokey-cokey, oh the hokey-cokey.
Oh, the hokey-cokey, knees bend, arms stretch,
Rah-rah-rah!
You put your right arm in…..
You put your left leg in…..
You put your whole self in……………..
•Sing the song doing the actions. Sing it again going faster.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to identify the correct body part, put it in and out, shake it, turn around, bend knees, stretch arms, and follow the sequence of the song.

Attempts most actions including putting the correct arm or leg in and out, shaking movements, turning around, bending knees and stretching arms. May need reminders to follow instructions accurately or keep pace as the song becomes faster.

Correctly performs most movements in sequence, including identifying left and right body parts, shaking, turning, bending and stretching. Maintains good coordination and control and follows the faster version with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions in time with the music. Correctly identifies left and right body parts, puts them in and out, shakes them with control, turns around safely, bends knees and stretches arms appropriately, adapts confidently to the increased speed, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting to 5.

exercises.title: I'm A Little Teapot
exercises.instructions:
I'm a little teapot, short and stout,
Here's my handle, (Bend arm hand on hip to make handle.)
Here's my spout. (Hold out other arm to make spout.)
When I see the teacups, hear me shout, (Cup both hands to your mouth.)
Tip me up and pour me out.
(Put back handle and spout and tip to one side.)
Stand feet together, arms by the side. Count 5,4,3,2,1.
Make the handle and spout with your arms and tip down and back again three times. Change sides and repeat.
Walk along a straight line, use arms to balance.
Walk backward along the line looking straight ahead.
Lie on your back and kick your legs in the air.
Be still, eyes closed. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to make the teapot shape, tip safely to the side, walk along the line, walk backwards, kick legs in the air, and remain still at the end.

Attempts most actions including making the handle and spout, tipping from side to side, balancing on the line, walking backwards and kicking legs. May need reminders to maintain balance, control movements, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Makes clear teapot shapes on both sides, tips and returns to standing safely, walks forwards and backwards along the line with reasonable balance, kicks legs with coordination, and settles quietly with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions. Creates the handle and spout clearly on both sides, tips smoothly and with good body control, walks forwards and backwards along the line while maintaining balance, kicks legs rhythmically when lying on their back, follows the complete sequence independently, and remains still with eyes closed while counting to 5.

exercises.title: Mary Had a Little Lamb
exercises.instructions:
Mary had a little lamb,
Little lamb,
Little lamb.
Mary had a little lamb,
Its fleece was white as snow.
And everywhere that Mary went,
Mary went,
Mary went,
And everywhere that Mary went
The lamb was sure to go.
It followed her to school one day,
School one day,
School one day.
It followed her to school one day
Which was against the rule.
Sing the rhyme together.
Jump on the spot
Jump forwards using your arms to help you.
Play follow my leader – Mix walking, skipping, jumping.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some parts of the rhyme and attempts a few movements. Needs significant support to jump on the spot, jump forwards, follow a leader, change between walking, skipping and jumping, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including jumping on the spot, jumping forwards and following the leader. May need reminders to coordinate arm movements, maintain balance, change between movement types, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Jumps on the spot and forwards with reasonable coordination, follows the leader successfully, changes between walking, skipping and jumping with minimal support, and lies quietly on their back while counting to 5.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Jumps on the spot and forwards with good control and balance, uses arms effectively to aid movement, confidently follows the leader, smoothly changes between walking, skipping and jumping, follows instructions throughout, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting to 5.

exercises.title: London Bridge
exercises.instructions:
London Bridge is falling down,
Falling down, falling down,
London Bridge is falling down,
My fair lady. (Chorus)
Build it up with sticks and stones,
Sticks and stones, sticks and stones,
Build it up with sticks and stones,
My fair lady.
Repeat Chorus
Sing the rhyme together.
Stretch up tall.
Stretch out wide.
Stretch your fingers (splay)
Make a fist. (Thumb on top)
Build a tower putting alternate hands on top of each other.
Now take the tower down (alternate hands).
Get down on to your hands and knees – make a bridge with your back.
Roll over and over – one way and back again.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to stretch in different directions, make hand shapes, build and take down the tower, form a bridge shape on hands and knees, roll safely, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including stretching tall and wide, splaying fingers, making a fist, building the tower, forming a bridge, and rolling. May need reminders to use alternate hands, control body movements, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Stretches in all directions, demonstrates the hand movements accurately, builds and takes down the tower using alternate hands, forms a bridge shape effectively, rolls safely in both directions, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Demonstrates full stretches, clear finger and fist movements, builds and dismantles the tower smoothly using alternate hands, creates a strong bridge shape on hands and knees, rolls with good body control in both directions, follows the complete sequence confidently, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: Two Little Fluffy Birds
exercises.instructions:
Two little fluffy birds sitting on a wall,
One named Peter, And one named Paul.
Fly away Peter,
Fly away Paul.
Come back Peter,
Come back Paul.
Sing the rhyme together using your index fingers to be Peter and Paul.
Flap you hands up and down from the wrist – both up and both down.
Now flap one hand up with the other down.
Raise your arms out to the side (shoulder height) – hold for 3, 2, 1
Slowly lower your arms. Repeat 3 times.
Fly around the room flapping your arms.
Stop and rest on the wall. Repeat several times.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some parts of the rhyme and attempts a few actions. Needs significant support to use index fingers as Peter and Paul, flap hands from the wrist, raise arms to shoulder height, fly around the room, stop on command, and rest quietly on their tummy.

Attempts most actions including finger movements, wrist flapping, raising and lowering arms, and flying around the room. May need reminders to coordinate movements, hold arms at shoulder height, stop to rest on the wall, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Uses index fingers effectively to represent Peter and Paul, coordinates wrist flapping movements, holds arms at shoulder height for the count, flies around the room safely, stops and rests appropriately, and lies quietly on their tummy while counting to 5 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Uses index fingers expressively as Peter and Paul, demonstrates controlled wrist movements, raises and lowers arms smoothly while maintaining shoulder height, flies around the room with good coordination and body awareness, responds promptly to stop and rest cues, and settles calmly on their tummy while counting to 5.

exercises.title: Little Bo Peep
exercises.instructions:
Little Bo-peep has lost her sheep,
And doesn't know where to find them.
Leave them alone and they'll come home,
Bringing their tails behind them.
Little Bo Peep fell fast asleep,
And dreamt she heard them running.
When she awoke she laughed and she joked,
As she could see them coming.
Sing the rhyme together.
Turn your head slowly from side to side (pretend you are looking for the sheep).
Walk around the room – change direction on signal (clap of hands).
Nod your head forwards and backwards (Yes, you can see the sheep).
Pretend to be a sheep and crawl around the room.
Crawl forwards and backwards.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to turn their head, change direction when walking, nod appropriately, crawl forwards and backwards, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including searching for the sheep by turning the head, walking and changing direction on a signal, nodding the head, and crawling. May need reminders to respond to the clap, coordinate movements, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Turns the head slowly from side to side, changes direction when signalled, nods appropriately, crawls forwards and backwards with coordination, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Demonstrates controlled head movements when searching for the sheep, responds promptly to directional changes while walking, nods clearly, crawls forwards and backwards with good coordination and body control, follows the complete sequence confidently, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: Hey Diddle Diddle
exercises.instructions:
Hey diddle, diddle,
The cat and the fiddle,
The cow jumped over the moon.
The little dog laughed to see such fun,
And the dish ran away with the spoon.
Say the rhyme together.
Run on the spot – then around the room. Stop on signal. Change direction. (Dish running away)
Jump up and down as high as you can.
Take three jumps forward….and three jumps back.
Stretch up high to the moon – make your hands into stars.
Wave your arms from side to side.
Make a fist with your thumb on top – swing your arms up and down.
Walk slowly around the room – stop on signal.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to run, stop on a signal, change direction, jump forwards and backwards, stretch upwards, wave arms, swing arms, and rest quietly on their tummy.

Attempts most actions including running, stopping on signal, changing direction, jumping up and down, taking jumps forwards and backwards, stretching to the moon, waving arms and walking slowly. May need reminders to maintain control, follow instructions, or complete the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Responds to signals appropriately, changes direction when required, jumps forwards and backwards with coordination, stretches and waves arms effectively, swings arms rhythmically, and rests quietly on their tummy while counting to 5 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Runs safely and responds promptly to stop and direction-change signals, jumps high and with good balance, completes forward and backward jumps confidently, stretches fully towards the moon, creates star shapes with hands, waves and swings arms with control, walks slowly when required, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly on their tummy while counting to 5.

exercises.title: Jelly On The Plate
exercises.instructions:
(Wobble your body.)
Jelly on the plate,
Jelly on the plate,
Wibble, wobble, wibble, wobble,
Jelly on the plate.
(Wobble your arms.)
Wobble both your arms,
Wobble both your arms,
Wibble, wobble, wibble, wobble,
Wobble both your arms.
(Wobble your legs.)
Wobble both your legs,
Wobble both your legs,
Wibble, wobble, wibble, wobble,
Wobble both your legs.
(Wobble your body.)
Jelly on the plate,
Jelly on the plate,
Wibble, wobble, wibble, wobble,
Jelly on the plate.
Sing the song doing the movements.
Lie on your tummy and wriggle . . . turn on to your back and have a good wriggle! Lie still. Close your Eyes. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some of the wobbling and wriggling actions but needs significant support to move different body parts separately, change positions from tummy to back, and lie still at the end.
Attempts most actions including wobbling the body, arms and legs, and wriggling on the tummy and back. May need reminders to follow the sequence, control movements, or change positions independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Wobbles body parts as instructed, wriggles effectively on both tummy and back, changes position smoothly, follows the sequence with minimal support, and lies still with eyes closed while counting to 5.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Clearly wobbles the body, arms and legs, demonstrates coordinated wriggling movements on both tummy and back, changes positions smoothly and safely, follows the complete sequence confidently, and settles calmly with eyes closed while counting to 5.

exercises.title: The Grand Old Duke of York
exercises.instructions:
Sing the song doing the actions.
Oh the Grand old Duke of York,
(March on the spot and keep marching.)
He had ten thousand men,
(Stretch out fingers and thumbs.)
He marched them up to the top of the hill,
(Reach up high.)
And he marched them down again.
(Reach down low.)
When they were up, they were up,
(Reach up.)
When they were down, they were down.
(Reach down.)
When they were only half way up,
(Reach half way.)
They were neither up,
(Reach up….
Nor down…….and down)
March on the spot swinging your arms.
March around the room.
Wave your arm in a semi-circle in front of you – backwards and forwards - to make a hill.
Now wave the other arm.
Stretch up high and then bend forwards to make a hill with your back.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2,1
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to march, coordinate arm movements, reach up and down, form hill shapes with arms and body, follow directions around the room, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including marching on the spot, swinging arms, reaching high and low, making hill shapes with the arms, and bending forwards. May need reminders to maintain rhythm, follow the sequence, or move safely around the room.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Marches rhythmically on the spot and around the room, reaches accurately to different levels, creates hill shapes with arms and body, follows the sequence with minimal support, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Marches with good rhythm and coordination, swings arms effectively, reaches confidently to high, low and halfway positions, creates clear hill shapes using arms and body, follows the complete sequence independently, moves safely around the room, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: Jack and Jill
exercises.instructions:
Jack and Jill went up the hill,
To fetch a bucket of water.
Jack ran instead then bumped his head,
And Jill came tumbling after.
Up they got, and home they shot,
As fast as Jack could make her.
Jack went to bed and bound his head,
With vinegar and brown paper
Sing the rhyme together.
Finger walk up your arms to fetch a pail of water.
Slide your fingers down your arm for Jack falling.
Roll your arms over and over each other as Jill tumbles down.
Lie on the floor and clasp your hands above your head,
Roll over and over one way and then back again.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to march, coordinate arm movements, reach up and down, form hill shapes with arms and body, follow directions around the room, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including marching on the spot, swinging arms, reaching high and low, making hill shapes with the arms, and bending forwards. May need reminders to maintain rhythm, follow the sequence, or move safely around the room.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Marches rhythmically on the spot and around the room, reaches accurately to different levels, creates hill shapes with arms and body, follows the sequence with minimal support, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Marches with good rhythm and coordination, swings arms effectively, reaches confidently to high, low and halfway positions, creates clear hill shapes using arms and body, follows the complete sequence independently, moves safely around the room, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: The Wheels on the Bus
exercises.instructions:
The wheels on the bus go round and round,
Round and round, round.
The wheels on the bus go round and round
All day long.
The children on the bus go chatter, chatter, chatter
Chatter, chatter, chatter, chatter, chatter, chatter.
The children on the bus go chatter, chatter, chatter
All day long.
The wipers on the bus go swish, swish, swish
Swish, swish, swish, swish, swish, swish
The wipers on the bus go swish, swish, swish,
All day long.
The horn on the bus goes beep, beep, beep,
Beep, beep, beep,
Beep, beep, beep.
The horn on the bus goes beep, beep, beep.
All day long. (*Repeat All Verses)
Sing the song together doing the actions.
Stand up and pretend to drive the bus around the room. Turn the steering wheel one way and then the other.
Stop and go on the signal.
Move one arm in a circle to make a big wheel.
Now turn the other arm to make a big wheel.
Move both arms together to make big wheels.
Stand feet together with arms by your side. Look straight ahead and count to 5.
Nod your head up and down to the people on the bus.
Shake your head from side to side to tell the children to be quiet.
Pretend to get off the bus and skip home.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to pretend to steer the bus, respond to stop and go signals, make wheel movements with the arms, nod and shake the head appropriately, skip, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including steering, making wheel circles with one or both arms, responding to signals, nodding and shaking the head, and skipping. May need reminders to coordinate movements, maintain balance, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Steers the bus appropriately, responds to stop and go signals, creates clear wheel movements with both arms, demonstrates controlled head movements, skips with reasonable coordination, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Steers confidently while moving around the room, responds promptly to stop and go signals, creates smooth circular wheel movements with one arm and both arms together, nods and shakes the head appropriately, skips with good rhythm and balance, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
exercises.instructions:
Twinkle twinkle little star,
(Move fingers to twinkle like a star.)
How I wonder what you are.
(Stretch up tall and look at the sky.)
Up above the world so high, (turn around)
Like a diamond in the sky.
(Join hands above head, elbows bent to make a diamond.)
Twinkle twinkle little star,
(Lie on tummy raised up on elbows, look up to the sky.)
How I wonder what you are.
(Move head slowly from side to side.)
Sing the song together doing the actions.
Stand feet apart. Stretch up to the stars – arms out and head tipped back.
Close in – arms crossed with hands on shoulders, head down.
Repeat 3 times.
Shooting Stars: Shoot your arm out and make a star with your fingers. Make a fist with your thumb on top when you pull your arm back. Shoot stars in all directions.
Run around the room. On the signal stop and make shooting stars.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to pretend to steer the bus, respond to stop and go signals, make wheel movements with the arms, nod and shake the head appropriately, skip, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including steering, making wheel circles with one or both arms, responding to signals, nodding and shaking the head, and skipping. May need reminders to coordinate movements, maintain balance, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Steers the bus appropriately, responds to stop and go signals, creates clear wheel movements with both arms, demonstrates controlled head movements, skips with reasonable coordination, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Steers confidently while moving around the room, responds promptly to stop and go signals, creates smooth circular wheel movements with one arm and both arms together, nods and shakes the head appropriately, skips with good rhythm and balance, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: Hickory Tickory Tock
exercises.instructions:
Hickory, tickory, tock, (Point finger from side to side).
The mouse ran up the clock. (Use fingers to run up arm.)
The clock struck one, (Point with finger.)
The mouse ran down. (Use fingers to run down arm.)
Hickory, tickory, tock. (Point finger and wave side to side.)
Sing the song together doing the actions.
Stand straight, feet apart. Make the long hand of the clock – straight arm, point finger. Move the hand around the clock at five-minute intervals saying, 'Tick, tock.'
Now change arms and move around the clock.
Take short fast steps forward. Turn and go back to the starting point. Repeat in several directions.
Imagine you are the mouse and crawl around the room.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to point accurately, move fingers up and down the arm, make clock-hand movements, walk in different directions, crawl like a mouse, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including finger movements, making clock hands with the arms, taking short fast steps forwards and backwards, and crawling. May need reminders to coordinate movements, change direction appropriately, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Uses fingers effectively to represent the mouse, moves arms to create clock hands, steps forwards and backwards with coordination, crawls confidently in different directions, follows the sequence with minimal support, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Demonstrates precise finger movements, creates clear clock-hand actions with both arms, moves confidently in multiple directions using short fast steps, crawls smoothly like a mouse with good coordination and body control, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.

exercises.title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat
exercises.instructions:
Row, row, row your boat,
Gently down the stream.
Merrily, merrily, merrily, merrily,
Life is but a dream.
Row, row, row your boat,
Gently down the stream.
If you see a crocodile,
Don't forget to scream.
Sing the song together doing rowing actions.
Sit on the floor – knees bent, feet flat on the floor slightly apart, arms out to the side.
Rock side to side.
Hands out in front – rock forwards and backwards.
Stretch hands out in front – open and close touching the palms of the hands to make the crocodile's jaws. Change so the other hand is on top.
Skip around the room. Stop on the signal and throw your hands up in the air. Pretend you have seen the crocodile.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to perform the rowing movements, rock in different directions, make crocodile jaws with the hands, respond to signals, skip around the room, and settle quietly on their tummy.

Attempts most actions including rowing, rocking side to side and forwards and backwards, making crocodile jaws, skipping, and responding to the crocodile signal. May need reminders to coordinate movements, change hand positions, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Demonstrates coordinated rowing and rocking movements, changes hand positions to make crocodile jaws, skips with reasonable balance, responds appropriately to the signal, and rests quietly on their tummy while counting to 5 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Uses smooth and controlled rowing movements, rocks confidently in different directions, creates clear crocodile jaw actions with both hand positions, skips with good rhythm and balance, responds promptly to signals by stopping and raising hands, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly on their tummy while counting to 5.

exercises.title: Incy Wincy Spider
exercises.instructions:
Incy Wincy Spider,
Climbed up the water spout.
Down came the rain,
And washed the spider out.
Out came the sunshine,
And dried up all the rain.
Incy Wincey Spider,
Climbed up the spout again.
Sing the song together moving your fingers to make the spider.
Crawl on your hands and knees like a spider – go around and around your web.
Stand still feet apart: roll you head around one way and then the other. Nod forwards and backwards (What is going to fly into your web?)
Stand with a friend. Lift your arms and legs up and down to make the 8 legs of thespider.
Stand still feet together. Close your eyes and count to eight.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Imagine you are a spider with 8 legs. Count back from 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to make spider movements with the fingers, crawl on hands and knees, perform head movements, coordinate movements with a partner, stand still with eyes closed, and relax at the end of the activity.

Attempts most actions including finger spider movements, crawling, rolling and nodding the head, partner activities, and standing still to count. May need reminders to coordinate movements, maintain balance, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Uses fingers effectively to represent the spider, crawls confidently around the space, performs head movements smoothly, works cooperatively with a partner to create the spider's legs, stands still while counting to eight, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 8 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Demonstrates precise finger movements, coordinated crawling, controlled head rolling and nodding, effective cooperation with a partner, maintains balance and stillness while counting with eyes closed, follows the complete sequence confidently, and settles calmly on their back while counting back from 8 to 1.

exercises.title: Half A Pound of Pudding Rice
exercises.instructions:
Half a pound of pudding rice,
Half a pound of treacle,
That's the way the money goes,
POP!
Goes the weasel.
Sing the song together. Clap your hands together when you sing, 'Pop!'
Sing the song and jump when you get to 'Pop!'
Sing the song and hop when you get to 'Pop!'
Walk along a straight line – use your arms to balance.
Jump over a line or rope from side to side.
March around the room – lie down on your back when you hear the signal. Lift up one leg high and put it down.
Lift up the other leg high and put it down.
Pretend to be on your bike cycling.
Lie down on your tummy and rest. Count to 5.
levels: Joins in with some actions but needs significant support to clap, jump or hop on cue, walk along a line, jump sideways over a line, respond to signals, lift legs independently, pedal cycling legs, and settle quietly on their tummy.

Attempts most actions including clapping, jumping, hopping, balancing along a line, jumping sideways, marching, leg lifts and cycling movements. May need reminders to respond at the correct time, maintain balance, coordinate movements, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Responds appropriately to "Pop!", balances while walking along the line, jumps over the line with coordination, lifts each leg independently, pedals smoothly, follows signals with minimal support, and rests quietly on their tummy while counting to 5.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Claps, jumps and hops precisely on cue, walks along the line with good balance, jumps confidently from side to side, responds promptly to signals, demonstrates controlled leg lifts and cycling actions, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly on their tummy while counting to 5.

exercises.title: Pat-A-Cake
exercises.instructions:
Pat-a-cake,
Pat – a – cake,
Baker's man,
Bake me a cake as fast as you can.
Pat it,
And poke it,
And mark it with "B",
And put it in the oven for baby and me.
Say the rhyme clapping your hands to the rhythm.
Clap in all different directions – in front, behind, to the side, high and low.
Pretend you are holding a wooden spoon. Stir the cake mixture – big circles in front of you. Stir three times one way and then the other.
Change hands and stir the mixture – three times one way and three times the other.
Imagine there is a circle in front of you (or use a hoop).
Walk around the circle – one way and then the other.
Jump into the middle of the circle and out the other side.
Hop around the circle.
Sit in the middle of the circle – pat your head, pat your knee, pat your foot.
Lie on your back, eyes closed. Count back from 5, 4, 3, 2, 1
levels: Joins in with some clapping and movement activities but needs significant support to clap in different positions, stir using both hands, move around the circle, jump, hop, identify body parts, and settle quietly on their back.

Attempts most actions including clapping in various directions, stirring movements, walking around the circle, jumping in and out, hopping, and patting different body parts. May need reminders to coordinate movements, change direction, maintain balance, or follow the sequence independently.

Performs most actions correctly and with control. Claps accurately in different positions, stirs smoothly with both hands, walks and hops around the circle with reasonable balance, jumps in and out successfully, correctly pats head, knee and foot, and lies quietly on their back while counting back from 5 with minimal support.

Independently and accurately performs all actions throughout the activity. Demonstrates coordinated clapping in all directions, controlled stirring movements with both hands, confident walking, jumping and hopping around the circle, accurately identifies and pats different body parts, follows the complete sequence independently, and settles calmly on their back with eyes closed while counting back from 5 to 1.
